title: Anth.us Papyrus: 4 published Gatsby src/pages URLs have no page in the port (/engage/, /reading/, /research/, /decision-models/)
description:
Four URLs that production anth.us publishes in its sitemap have NO equivalent page in the Papyrus port, so they will 404 on cutover. This is a content/port gap, not a URL-namespace bug, and it is out of scope for PR #3 (https://github.com/AnthusAI/Anth.us-Papyrus/pull/3) — filing so it is not lost.

## The URLs
All four return 200 on production right now (verified live) and all four are in `https://anth.us/sitemap-0.xml`:

- `/decision-models/`
- `/engage/`
- `/reading/`
- `/research/`

## Why the port cannot redirect them
They are Gatsby pages from `Anth.us/src/pages/*.js`, NOT MDX files in `AnthusAI/anthus-site-content`. The Papyrus port discovers content only from the content submodule and hand-writes six bespoke pages (`index`, `about`, `ai-solutions`, `ryan`, `platform` index, `articles` index, plus `404`). There is nothing in the port for these four to redirect TO, so no 301 can be written. The redirect generator correctly emits no rule and they fall through to the catch-all 404.

Note `/engage` is also the single biggest unresolved internal link target in the corpus — 12 refs across the content point at it. On production those resolve; in the port they do not.

The local `/Users/home/Projects/Anth.us` checkout is older than production and has only `404.js about.js ai-solutions.js index.js platform.js ryan.js` in `src/pages/`, so these four were added to production after that checkout. Confirm against the live repo before acting.

## Options (not decided)
1. Port each as a bespoke page in `web/anthus_pages.py`, same as `about`/`ryan`.
2. Author them into the content repo as MDX, which gives them `/articles/<slug>/` URLs and then 301s from the bare-root shape for free.
3. Accept the 404s and redirect them somewhere sensible (e.g. `/engage/` -> the contact form URL already in `anthus_pages.CONTACT_URL`).

Needs Ryan's call on what these pages are for. Must be resolved BEFORE any promotion to the production domain, not before the staging review.

comments.text: Ryan decided 2026-10-03: ADD the missing pages (port /engage/, /reading/, /research/, /decision-models/ as pages). Confirm content against the live production repo/site first; the local Anth.us checkout predates them.
